A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ModernVBERT study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training experiments, retrieval and classification evaluations, design ablations, and CPU latency measurements, including additional experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds fine-tuned SigLIP comparisons, image-processing latency measurements, and GPU query-encoding and throughput results.

M1.justification: The early-fusion architecture, MLM alignment, LoRA adaptation, contrastive objective, late-interaction scoring, and final ModernVBERT training recipe remain unchanged. Expanded descriptions of image tiling, padding, and pixel shuffling document the existing procedure rather than establish a new method.

E1.justification: Training sources and substantive evaluation coverage remain unchanged: ViDoRe, natural-image retrieval and classification, and NanoBEIR text retrieval. The added efficiency measurements and SigLIP controls do not introduce new data domains, languages, or retrieval tasks.

E2.justification: Figure 3 replaces the off-the-shelf SigLIP comparison with fine-tuned SigLIP2-FT and SigLIP2-FT Large controls. The original comparison is retained and expanded with the larger off-the-shelf model in Appendix C.1. The CPU latency comparison additionally reports measurements for MoCa-3B, GME-Qwen2, VLM2Vec, E5-V, and Jina-v4, previously marked unavailable. The main retrieval leaderboard otherwise retains its comparator set.

E3.justification: CPU timing changes from 1,000 queries averaging 60 characters on Google Colab to 649 NanoBEIR queries averaging 147.5 characters on high-memory CPUs, with batch size 1. New protocols cover 100-image CPU/L4 timing and H100 online and batched inference. Section 2.2 also corrects 118M pairs per source to 118k, consistent with Table 7 already in v1; this is a reported-setting correction, not evidence of changed training data or rerunning.

E4.justification: Appendix C.6.1 adds targeted analysis of image resolution and pixel-shuffling trade-offs in token counts and encoding latency. The revised SigLIP experiment strengthens training and model-size controls for the modality-alignment comparison. Existing attention-mask, training-mixture, model-merging, and curriculum ablations are retained.

E5.justification: v1 reports latency averages without uncertainty. v2 Tables 11–12 introduce mean and standard-deviation reporting across images or queries for CPU and unbatched GPU timing, while explicitly omitting standard deviations for batched throughput. Neither version reports training-seed uncertainty; these additions do not establish more independent training runs.

E6.justification: Substantial new efficiency results and fine-tuned baseline scores are reported. Figure 3 retains the encoder's 43.8 document score but adds SigLIP2-FT scores of 37.7 and 43.0; the base-comparator margin is therefore 6.1 rather than 10.9 against the original off-the-shelf control. ColModernVBERT's CPU latency changes from 32 to 20 ms under different conditions, with new GPU and image-processing results. Main retrieval scores, including its 81.2/56.0 ViDoRe results, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The language-modeling losses, InfoNCE objective, cosine similarity, and late-interaction equations are unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs. The added pixel-shuffling discussion explains existing computational behavior without introducing new formal reasoning.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a controlled study of visual-retriever design and a compact 250M encoder competitive with models roughly ten times larger. The rewritten abstract emphasizes RAG and CPU efficiency, but these deployment benefits were already advanced in v1. The stated contributions and conclusion retain their substantive scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds qualifications about RAM requirements and offloading costs for larger models. Appendix C.6.2 interprets GPU latency through model depth, hardware-aware architecture, FlashAttention, and sequence packing. The earlier limitations concerning small model scales and English-only evaluation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds resizing/padding and visual-token details, plus benchmarking information on hardware, precision, loading only text parameters, and adaptive batching. Appendix A.1 replaces a future code-release statement with a concrete repository address. Table 3 corrects GME-Qwen2's reported size from 3.75B to 8.29B. The existing training hyperparameters and resource table remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The rewritten introduction adds references on dense passage retrieval, RAG, text embeddings, and retrieval-augmented visual question answering. References to LLM2Vec, repetition-based embeddings, and the original SigLIP paper are removed. This shifts introductory emphasis toward practical document search without substantially changing positioning against generative VLM retrievers and late-interaction methods.

P1.justification: The abstract and much of the introduction are substantially rewritten around industrial retrieval, RAG, and OCR-pipeline limitations. Method explanations are expanded, terminology is edited throughout, and the appendices gain dedicated comparison and latency subsections. The detailed author-contribution and acknowledgment sections are removed.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redesigned with fine-tuned baseline series, while the original comparison is expanded and relocated to appendix Figure 7. A new token/hidden-size trade-off plot and two latency tables provide substantial additional visual evidence. Table 3 revises units and annotations, Table 9 changes to a text-wrapped layout, and retained appendix figures are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 provides fairer SigLIP controls, broader efficiency evidence with variability reporting, clearer implementation details, and a correction to the misleading 118M training-pair statement. These strengthen support for the retained findings without changing the central method or retrieval results. The improvement is limited by remaining reporting ambiguity: Section 4.2 specifies 2 TB CPU RAM while Table 12 specifies 1 TB, and the revised latencies cannot demonstrate same-setting speed gains.
